observations.behavior: Adds client-side normalization of channel names as the user types, converting spaces and other separators to hyphens.
observations.posthog_connection: Reduces manual cleanup effort for users creating a workspace or context in PostHog Desktop; prevents invalid characters from reaching backend validation.

observations.behavior: Adds an onBlur handler that re-normalizes input before losing focus.
observations.posthog_connection: Ensures consistent naming regardless of typing interruptions, supporting reliable downstream processing without requiring explicit save actions.

observations.behavior: Replaces simple trimming with full name normalization including separator replacement and case folding.
observations.posthog_connection: Changes stored identifiers to be directory-safe and unique across casing variations, potentially reducing duplicate contexts and improving compatibility with filesystem-based storage.

review.reason: The change introduces substantive client-side behavior: normalizing channel names while the user types and on blur, plus adding descriptive help text. This is not merely documentation or a trivial test addition; it changes how users interact with PostHog Desktop's workspace creation flow. The implementation includes helper functions and updated UI bindings, demonstrating bounded capability improvement rather than systemic architectural overhaul.
review.posthog_relevance: Helps end-users create cleaner, compatible context/workspace names in PostHog Desktop, reducing configuration errors and potential duplicates caused by inconsistent naming conventions.
review.uncertainty: Without seeing backend compatibility handling or broader deployment context, cannot assess whether this could cause issues downstream if normalized names conflict with existing resources.
